issue.title: New semantic analyzer: conflict between direct import and add_submodules_to_parent_modules()

labels.name: semantic-analyzer
labels.description: Problems that happen during semantic analysis

issue.body:
Consider this test case:
```
[case testNewAnalyzerConfusingImport]
# flags: --follow-imports=skip --ignore-missing-imports
# cmd: mypy -m other a.b a
[file a/__init__.py]
[file a/b/__init__.py]
import other
import a.b.a
import a.b.c

[file other.py]
from a.b.a import foo
[builtins fixtures/module.pyi]
[out]
```
It passes with the old analyzer, but there is a subtle conflict between what should name `a` 
point to in the symbol table of `a.b`: to module `a`, or to module `a.b.a`? The code that handles this is a bit fragile, and depending on the order of processing of modules may fail in new analyzer with:
```
tmp/a/b/__init__.py:2: error: Name 'a' already defined (possibly by an import)
tmp/a/b/__init__.py:3: error: Name 'a' already defined (possibly by an import)
```
I am not sure what to do about this. Should we try to avoid this error (maybe at least for case when one of the module is not in build like in the test above)?

issue.title: New semantic analyzer: only create each SymbolNode once

labels.name: semantic-analyzer
labels.description: Problems that happen during semantic analysis

issue.body:
Currently we can create a symbol node multiple times (once per iteration), which is risky since we don't want to risk having different references to a particular name pointing to different nodes. For example, class-based TypedDict definitions may create multiple `TypeInfo` objects per definition.

I think that for most things we can treat the definition as complete once we've successfully created a symbol table node, and further iterations would skip the definition, as there's nothing more to do. 

Normal class definitions should not have this problem, but we should verify that these work as expected:

* `Var` nodes
* TypedDict (as discussed above)
* Named tuples
* Type variables
* Type aliases
* NewTypes
* Enums

body:
It looks like the approach taken in #6630 isn't workable and needs to be replaced with something more general. The new semantic analyzer relies on only creating a non-placeholder symbol node once per name (#6300) and submodules shouldn't deviate from this, since any deviations increase complexity and likely cause bugs.

My current idea is that implicit submodule references shouldn't be added to symbol tables. Instead, we could look them up from a separate "module scope". If a name is defined in a module, we use that. Otherwise, we fall back to the module dictionary to check if the name refers to a module. 

To implement this logic, we'd need to keep track of where a definition is valid using the line number of the definition.

There are various edge cases that are still unclear to me and need more thought.

> My current idea is that implicit submodule references shouldn't be added to symbol tables. Instead, we could look them up from a separate "module scope". If a name is defined in a module, we use that. Otherwise, we fall back to the module dictionary to check if the name refers to a module.

Generally I like this idea. I was thinking about something similar, but even more global. There is another case where we want to have essentially two nodes in the same symbol table under the same name: the `-redefinition` thing. (Yet another will be conditional imports currently unsupported.)

We can make a symbol table essentially a mapping from names to a deque of nodes, but `__getitem__` will always return the leading one. There will be a method to access all of them. Plus two methods to push on either end, depending on whether we want to shadow existing name (like with named tuples or plugins), or not (like for redefinitions or for implicit imports).

Yet another related thing to consider is `--allow-redefinition`. If we are going to move towards something more SSA-like (e.g. allowing conditional redefinitions), then the current scheme with variable renaming with primes, `x`, `x'`, `x''`, etc., might not work well. We will need to be able to record that in
```python
if bool():
    x = int()
else:
    x = str()
foo(x)
```
the last `x` may refer to either `Var` node. With the deque logic this seems possible to address.

issue.title: New semantic analyzer: don't add submodules to symbol tables
issue.body:
Previously we added each submodule implicitly to the the symbol table of
the parent package. This PR removes this and instead we look up names from
the modules dictionary if they aren't found in the symbol table. The change
only affects the new semantic analyzer.

This provides the foundation that should make it easier to fix #6828. It also 
arguably cleans up the code.

Also refactor some related code to avoid duplication.

This isn't a pure refactor since some error messages are slightly different.

issue.title: New semantic analyzer: fix ambiguity between submodule and local def
issue.body:
Now imports are biased to target the submodule of current package,
but elsewhere a local definition with the same name as a submodule 
takes precedence.  Even though this doesn't quite reflect what 
happens at runtime, this seems to cover the typical use cases well, 
and the implementation is simple.

Fixes #6828.
